title: Drip Irrigation Systems & Efficiency Management
irrigation_methods: Micro-drip irrigation via inline drippers or online emitters
crop_wise_schedules: Banana (every 1-2 days, 25-35 L/plant), Sugarcane (3-5 days), Cotton (3-4 days), Grapes (2 days), Pomegranate (2 days)
water_saving_techniques: Saves 40-60% water compared to flood irrigation. Allows direct root-zone fertigation, reduces weed growth by keeping non-crop soil dry, and prevents fungal foliage diseases.
content: Drip irrigation delivers water and soluble liquid nutrients directly to the plant root zone at low discharge rates (2-4 LPH). It maintains uniform soil moisture, prevents waterlogging, and minimizes evaporative losses.
source: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) Manual

title: Sprinkler Irrigation System Guide
irrigation_methods: Overhead pressurized sprinkler nozzles simulating natural rainfall
crop_wise_schedules: Wheat (every 10-12 days), Groundnut (8-10 days), Mustard (12-15 days), Pulses (10-14 days)
water_saving_techniques: Saves 30-40% water compared to surface flooding. Ideal for undulating or sandy soils where surface levelling is difficult.
content: Sprinkler systems distribute water under pressure through pipes and rotating nozzles over the crop canopy. Excellent for sandy soils, oilseeds, wheat, and pulses. Avoid operating under strong wind conditions.
source: ICAR Central Institute of Agricultural Engineering

title: Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) for Paddy Rice
irrigation_methods: Controlled intermittent flooding using a perforated field water tube (Pani Pipe)
crop_wise_schedules: Allow water level in field tube to drop 15cm below soil surface before re-flooding field to 5cm depth. Keep field flooded continuously only during flowering stage.
water_saving_techniques: Reduces irrigation water consumption by 35% without reducing rice yield. Significantly cuts methane emissions from paddy fields.
content: Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) is a smart water-saving technology for lowland rice. A 30cm long, 15cm wide perforated PVC pipe is placed in the paddy field to observe water depth below the surface.

title: Furrow & Basin Irrigation Management
irrigation_methods: Surface gravity irrigation using alternating ridges and furrows or circular tree basins
crop_wise_schedules: Maize (every 8-10 days in summer), Cotton (every 10-12 days), Fruit Orchards (every 7-10 days)
water_saving_techniques: Alternate furrow irrigation (watering every second furrow) cuts water use by 30-40% while maintaining yield.
content: Furrow irrigation is widely used for row crops like maize, cotton, and vegetables. Water flows along narrow channels (furrows) between crop ridges, infiltrating sideways into root zones without submerging plant stems.

title: Mango Irrigation & Water Management Guide
content:
Regular watering is recommended till establishment. Under conventional irrigation systems, weekly irrigation is essential. However, under micro-irrigation the requirement is restricted to one-third of the water required for conventional method.
Intercropping
Short duration crops like legumes, vegetables, groundnut etc. can be raised during pre- bearing age.
